learning_intro_title: AWS IoT Registry APIs - AWS IoT Device Management
learning_intro_content: The AWS IoT Registry is like a central database that keeps track of all your IoT devices (Things), how they're organized (Thing Groups), device templates (Thing Types), and security certificates. These APIs let you manage your entire IoT device fleet programmatically. Understanding these operations is key to building scalable IoT solutions!

list_things.title: List Things - Device Discovery
list_things.content: The list_things API grabs all your IoT devices (Things) from your account. This is super useful for keeping track of your device inventory, monitoring how big your fleet is, and finding devices by their attributes. You can use pagination and filtering to handle even large device fleets efficiently!
list_things.next: Let's call the list_things API with different options

list_certificates.title: List Certificates - Security Inventory
list_certificates.content: X.509 certificates are the backbone of IoT device security. Each certificate uniquely identifies a device and enables secure communication with AWS IoT Core. This API helps you check your security setup, track certificate lifecycle, and spot devices that might need certificate rotation.
list_certificates.next: Let's retrieve all certificates and check out their security properties

list_thing_groups.title: List Thing Groups - Device Organization
list_thing_groups.content: Thing Groups help you organize your IoT devices hierarchically - kind of like folders for files! They let you do bulk operations, inherit policies, and group devices logically by location, function, or any business criteria. This is really important for managing large-scale IoT deployments.
list_thing_groups.next: Let's explore your Thing Groups and see how they're organized

list_thing_types.title: List Thing Types - Device Templates
list_thing_types.content: Thing Types are like templates that define categories of IoT devices. They act as blueprints that specify common attributes and behaviors for similar devices. For example, a 'SedanVehicle' type might define things like engine type and seating capacity. Thing Types help you organize your device fleet and make device management more standardized!
list_thing_types.next: Let's check out your Thing Types and their attribute schemas

describe_thing.title: Describe Thing - Device Details
describe_thing.content: The describe_thing API gives you complete information about a specific IoT device - including its attributes, Thing Type, version, and unique identifiers. This is really helpful for troubleshooting devices, managing configurations, and understanding how devices relate to each other in your IoT setup.
describe_thing.next: Let's look at detailed information for a specific Thing

describe_thing_group.title: Describe Thing Group - Group Management
describe_thing_group.content: Thing Group details show you how your IoT fleet is organized. You can see group properties, parent-child hierarchies, attached policies, and which devices are members. This info is really important for understanding access control, how policies are inherited, and your device organization strategies.
describe_thing_group.next: Let's examine the detailed properties of a specific Thing Group

describe_thing_type.title: Describe Thing Type - Template Analysis
describe_thing_type.content: Thing Type details show you the blueprint definition for device categories. You can check out searchable attributes, property constraints, and metadata that define how devices of this type should be structured. This helps make sure device registration is consistent and lets you query your fleet efficiently!
describe_thing_type.next: Let's analyze the schema and properties of a specific Thing Type

describe_endpoint.title: Describe Endpoint - Connection Discovery
describe_endpoint.content: IoT endpoints are the gateway URLs that your devices use to connect to AWS IoT Core. Different endpoint types serve different purposes: Data-ATS for device communication, CredentialProvider for authentication, and AWS IoT Jobs for device management. Understanding endpoints is key to getting your device connectivity configured correctly!
describe_endpoint.next: Let's discover the endpoint URL for device connections
